text:
jon: Heads-up — I found a confusing UX when trying to cancel a streaming generator in Go while our auth layer was doing a retry/refresh. Small snippet that triggered it below.

jon: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
client := NewClient(WithCreds(slowCreds{}))
gen, err := client.Generator(ctx, "tiny-model")
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

// start stream and cancel soon after
go func() { time.Sleep(120 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx)
if err != nil { log.Printf("start err: %v", err); return }
for p := range stream.Receive() { _ = p }
// observed: process leaks goroutines stuck in creds.Fetch and Stream() doesn't return fast
```

tess: Is the leak in our code path or in the user's creds impl? Looks like creds may be doing blocking I/O without a ctx.

marco: Repro'd. Our ServerHandshake currently calls creds.Token() synchronously and only wires up ctx select after the token returns — if creds blocks the Stream handshake goroutine can't see ctx.Done().

olga: Two ways to improve DX: (1) require creds.GetToken(ctx) so refreshes are cancelable; (2) add an explicit generator.Interrupt()/Abort() method that forces handshake cancellation even if creds is blocking. Both could be shipped together but with a compatibility plan.

jon: I sketched a minimal onboarding note proposing a pattern for sample apps while we migrate: use a handshake timeout + call gen.Interrupt() from another goroutine on cancel. Example snippet to put in docs: `ctx, ht := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second); defer ht()` then call `gen.Stream(ctx)` and in cancel path call `gen.Interrupt()`.

marco: For parity: Python/Node already make auth refresh cancellable. Changing the Go creds interface is breaking so we should provide a small compatibility wrapper that spawns the legacy token fetch in a goroutine and returns early on ctx cancel (with a distinct ErrAuthCanceled). That avoids leaking our internal handshake goroutine.

tess: Agreed. Short-term plan: 1) add ClientOption HandshakeTimeout default 5s; 2) add Generator.Interrupt() as an explicit aborting API; 3) add a compatibility shim for old creds that returns ErrAuthCanceled on ctx cancel; 4) update onboarding sample app and README to show the WithTimeout + Interrupt pattern.

ci-bot: [ci] Canary job noticed elevated goroutine counts in generator e2e. Filing INF-5007.

jon: Action items: I'll draft the README snippet and a small sample-app PR showing the correct cancel pattern; Marco will prototype the Interrupt() implementation; Olga will draft the shim and open a migration doc for changelog. Include a unit test that simulates slow creds + ctx cancel and asserts no leaking goroutines.

marco: One tiny API question: should Interrupt() be idempotent and safe to call after Stream() returns? I think yes — it should be a no-op if handshake already finished.

olga: Also add diagnostic text in the error returned when handshake fails: include "possible blocking credentials: use GetToken(ctx) or wrap with shim" so users can self-diagnose onboarding friction.

tess: Putting this in the SDK parity board for the sprint. Thanks everyone. :pray:
